Americans now owe a record $1.73 trillion on their cars — and more are falling behind.

The New York Fed's latest Household Debt report (Q3 2026, released Nov. 10) shows auto-loan balances hit $1.73 trillion, part of a record $19.1 trillion in total household debt. More borrowers slipped into early 30-day-late delinquency on both car loans and mortgages.

Why it's your money: a car payment is now one of the biggest fixed bills a household carries. When more people fall behind, lenders tighten — higher rates and bigger down payments for the next buyer, even one with good credit.

My take: debt at a record while people fall behind is the worrying part — the strain is landing on paychecks.

Are car payments eating too much of your monthly budget?

Source: New York Fed Household Debt & Credit Report, Q3 2026 (Nov. 10).

Target's sales fell again — and its stock is down about 35% this year.

Target reported third-quarter results this morning (Nov. 18): revenue slipped 1.6% to $25.27 billion, and it trimmed the top of its full-year profit forecast. The stock is down roughly 35% in 2026. (Target Q3 2026 earnings.)

Why it's your money: Target is a read on how regular shoppers feel. People are still buying essentials but pulling back on extras — the 'value economy' — right as the holiday season starts. When a big retailer flinches, it shows up in prices, promotions and seasonal hiring.

My take: a 1.6% dip sounds small, but for a retailer this size it means shoppers are picking carefully — expect deeper discounts chasing your dollar this Black Friday.

Are you cutting back on non-essentials this holiday season?

Source: Target Q3 2026 earnings, Nov. 18, 2026.
Educational only — not financial advice.
